description: Code, pre-registration, derived data and full results for a benchmark of probabilistic load forecasting across four PJM extreme-cold events (January 2014 polar vortex, February 2015 official-error anchor, December 2017 - January 2018 cold snap, December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott). Three forecaster families (quantile gradient boosting, linear-tree LightGBM, statistical location-scale) are combined with five conformal calibrators at a day-ahead horizon (primary) and a one-hour oracle horizon, and judged under strictly chronological evaluation against retrospective leave-one-event-out transfer, under a protocol and formula specification frozen before any result was computed. Headline findings: uncalibrated 90% interval coverage collapses inside the events; no calibrator selected without the target event restores event-window coverage to nominal (0 of 18 cells pass the pre-registered repair judgement); retrospective transfer evaluation overstates the temperature-stratified Mondrian calibrators' event coverage by +11.6 pp and +21.2 pp relative to chronological evaluation (the pre-registered transfer-illusion configuration).
title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
